sections.hypothesis: Shorting a coin through the 30 days after its first perp listing, hedged with an equal long in BTC, makes money after costs and funding. It turns findings 18 (the coins lag the others by 15% over those 30 days) into a trade and shows what it would have earned. Hypothetical: Kestrel can't short (P5 parked; real perps are wholesale-only in Australia, retail shorting is CFDs at 2:1). A pass is recorded as needs-shorting and never traded until a licensed retail route exists.
sections.rationale: Who pays: as in does-a-perp-listing-mark-a-top (validated): before a perp exists, pessimists can't bet against a small coin; the listing lets them in after a run (+100% in the 30 days before, findings 18), and the coin lags. Outside evidence: Hale, Krishnamurthy, Kudlyak and Shultz (2018, FRBSF Economic Letter 2018-12): Bitcoin peaked the day CME futures began trading. Why hedged: the effect is relative (the coins' own 30-day return averaged +1.5%), so an unhedged short would mostly bet on the market; BTC is the hedge because it is one liquid position (against BTC the coins lagged -7.9% on average, -17.5% at the median). Disclosed: the rule comes straight from a study whose result is known, on the same coins and years, so this is not an independent test of the effect, only of whether it survives costs, funding, squeezes and a 3-slot limit; the holdout year's perp listings (2025-11 to 2026-10, any coin outside the locked confirmation half) are untouched and would be its clean test. Not a rejected family. Runs: one, one trial in the main log.
sections.rules: Events as does-a-perp-listing-mark-a-top v1 (exploration half plus BTC, ETH, SOL; first funding on or after 2020-01-02; 60+ days of spot before; the 30 days ending before 2025-11-01). At day 0's close, if a slot is free (at most 3 at once, first come first served; an event finding all 3 full is skipped and counted), open the trade at day 1's open: short the coin's USDT-M perp and buy BTC spot, each 2/9 of equity (so each slot uses 1/3 of equity: 2/9 in BTC and 1/9 as the perp's margin at 2:1). Hold to day 31's open, then close both. Weights are rebalanced daily to those targets (as kestrel short-study's simulator does). A day whose high reaches 1.5x its open closes the short out at that price (a margin call). A coin that stops trading is closed at its last close. Scored daily 2020-01-01 to 2025-10-30.
sections.parameters: Day 1 to day 31, 3 slots, 2/9 of equity a leg, BTC as the hedge, 1.5x close-out. Fixed before any trade was simulated; nothing else is tried.
sections.costs: Short leg: a Binance USDT-M perp, 5 bps taker per side (an assumption to check) plus the coin's spot half-spread band (no perp order-book history), and its real 8-hourly funding (a positive rate pays the short; new perps often carry negative funding, which charges it). Long leg: BTC spot as kestrel.toml (7.5 bps fee plus its band). Every change in weight pays. A CFD isn't modelled: small coins rarely have one.
